title: Bread, white with whole wheat swirl

content.title: About
content.content: Bread, white with whole wheat swirl is a classic wheat loaf that incorporates a decorative swirl of whole‑wheat flour into the dough. It combines the soft, airy crumb of a white loaf with a subtle nutty flavor from the whole‑wheat swirl.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The swirl is created by adding whole‑wheat flour in a spiral pattern during mixing.
White bread is often used as a sandwich base, while the whole‑wheat swirl adds extra nutrition.
Traditionally the loaf is baked with steam to achieve a crisp crust and a tender interior.
In some cultures the swirl symbolizes abundance and appears in festive breads.

items.title: Source of carbohydrates
items.content: The bread provides a quick source of energy through easily digestible carbs.

items.title: Contains whole grains
items.content: The whole‑wheat swirl adds fiber, B‑vitamins, and minerals.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Fiber from the whole‑grain swirl helps maintain regular bowel movements.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Because the base is primarily white flour, the loaf is low in fat.

items.title: Provides iron
items.content: The whole‑grain component increases iron content, important for blood health.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: Wheat bread contains gluten, which can trigger reactions in people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: White bread can raise blood sugar quickly, so individuals with diabetes should limit intake.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Some recipes add salt; those monitoring sodium should check the label.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Enjoy the bread fresh, toasted, or as the base for sandwiches, soups, and salads. The whole‑wheat swirl adds a pleasant flavor and texture, especially with cheese, ham, or vegetables.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the loaf in a paper bag or bread box at room temperature for up to 3 days. For longer storage, freeze in an airtight bag for up to 3 months. Thaw at room temperature or warm in the oven before serving.
